title: Random Signals and Noise
tagline: Probability for engineers, random processes, correlation and power spectra, noise and optimal filtering
summary: Noise limits every measurement and every communication link. This course reviews probability for engineers and develops random processes: stationarity, correlation functions and power spectral densities, random signals in linear systems, Gaussian and thermal noise, and the matched, Wiener and Kalman filters that extract signals from noise.

chapters.title: Probability for engineers
chapters.summary: Random variables, distributions, expectation, joint distributions and functions of random variables.

chapters.title: Random processes
chapters.summary: Ensembles and sample functions, mean and autocorrelation, stationarity and ergodicity.

chapters.title: Correlation and power spectral density
chapters.summary: Autocorrelation and cross-correlation, the Wiener–Khinchin theorem and power spectral densities.

chapters.title: Random signals in linear systems
chapters.summary: Output mean, correlation and spectrum of LTI systems driven by random inputs, and noise-equivalent bandwidth.

chapters.title: Gaussian processes and noise
chapters.summary: Gaussian processes, white noise, thermal and shot noise, and bandpass noise.

chapters.title: Optimal filtering
chapters.summary: The matched filter and the Wiener filter.

chapters.title: Estimation and the Kalman filter
chapters.summary: Minimum mean-square-error estimation, least squares and the discrete Kalman filter.
